creature.name: Mask of Norgorber

attacks.name: shortsword
attacks.damage: 3d6+14 slashing plus 1d6 persistent damage (see Aspect's Agony)

mid.name: Secretive Tattoos
entries: The mask keeps their faith tattoo hidden (typically by wearing gloves to cover the palm). To use it as a divine focus, they must first Interact to uncover the tattoo. The tattoo then stays uncovered until the mask Interacts to cover it up. A mask's faith tattoo only allows for the casting of harm. Upon the mask's death, the tattoo disappears.

mid.name: Aspect's Agony
entries: When a mask of Norgorber Strikes a foe with a weapon, they inflict an additional 1d6 persistent damage of a type determined by their aspect. As long as a creature is taking this persistent damage, they're off-guard.

mid.name: Sneak Attack
entries: A mask of Norgorber deals 2d6 extra precision damage to creatures who are off-guard.

mid.name: Aspect's Agony
entries: 1d6 persistent poison

mid.name: Evaporate Poison
entries: The mask blows out a breath and targets a creature within 30 feet that is currently poisoned or is taking persistent poison damage. The target must attempt a DC 37 Fortitude save as the mask attempts to transmute the poison afflicting them into toxic vapor.

mid.name: Critical Success
entries: The poison effect on the target immediately ends.

mid.name: Success
entries: The poison effect on the target immediately ends, but toxic vapor fills one of the target's adjacent squares, chosen by the mask. A creature in this square is exposed to brimstone fumes; the toxic vapor then vanishes.

mid.name: Failure
entries: As success, but the toxic vapor fills a 5-foot emanation around the target, exposing all creatures in the area (including the target) to brimstone fumes; the toxic vapor then vanishes.

mid.name: Critical Failure
entries: As failure, but the toxic vapor fills a 10-foot emanation around the target, and the poison effect or persistent poison damage the target is suffering does not end.

mid.name: Aspect's Agony
entries: 1d6 persistent bleed

mid.name: Invigorating Flense
entries: The mask makes a quick striking motion, as if slicing flesh with a small knife, and targets a creature within 30 feet. The target immediately takes 12d6 slashing and 5d6 persistent bleed damage (DC 37 basic Fortitude save), and the mask becomes quickened as long as the target continues to take persistent bleed damage. The mask can use the extra action only to Stride or Strike.

mid.name: Aspect's Agony
entries: 1d6 persistent void

mid.name: Steal Life
entries: The mask makes a quick plucking gesture as they attempt to steal a creature's life. The mask targets a living creature within 30 feet, inflicting 17d6 void damage (DC 37 basic Fortitude save). The mask gains temporary Hit Points equal to half the void damage the target takes (after applying resistances and the like), and loses any remaining temporary Hit Points after 24 hours.

mid.name: Aspect's Agony
entries: 1d6 persistent mental

mid.name: Insidious Secrets
entries: The mask whispers, then targets a creature within 30 feet. The target must then attempt a DC 37 Will save.

mid.name: Critical Success
entries: The target fails to hear the secret whispered and is unaffected.

mid.name: Success
entries: The mask whispers a horrific secret to the target, and though their mind recoils and forgets, the target still takes 8d6 mental damage and is frightened 1.

mid.name: Failure
entries: As failure, but 17d6 mental damage and frightened 2; the target is confused as long as they are frightened.

mid.name: Critical Failure
entries: As failure, but 30d6 mental damage and the target is confused for 1 minute.

When a powerful worshipper catches Norgorber's eye, he sometimes transforms that worshipper into one of his masks—supernatural incarnations who become powerful proxies to their god but sacrifice their free will. **[Recall Knowledge - Fiend](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)): DC 40 **[Recall Knowledge - Humanoid](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47)): DC 40 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 38 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 35 [Mask of Norgorber](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3748) **Source** [Pathfinder #206: Bring the House Down](/Sources.aspx?ID=247) pg. 84 **Perception** +32; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [_truesight_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1727) **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1); [_truespeech_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1728) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +31, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +28, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) +29, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) +30, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +30, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +30, [Norgorber Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +31, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) +28, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +27, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +33, [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) +31 **Str** +6 **Dex** +9 **Con** +5 **Int** +5 **Wis** +6 **Cha** +6 **Items** _+2 [greater striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2829) [shortsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=398)_, _[true faith tattoo](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2207)_, _+2 [resilient](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2786) [leather armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=41)_ --- **AC** 39 **Fort** +25 **Ref** +33 **Will** +28 **HP** 290 **Secretive Tattoos** The mask keeps their _faith tattoo_ hidden (typically by wearing gloves to cover the palm). To use it as a divine focus, they must first Interact to uncover the tattoo. The tattoo then stays uncovered until the mask Interacts to cover it up. The mask targets a living creature within 30 feet, inflicting 17d6 void damage (DC 37 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save). The mask gains temporary Hit Points equal to half the void damage the target takes (after applying resistances and the like), and loses any remaining temporary Hit Points after 24 hours. Aspect Of The Reaper These masks fracture trust and turn allies against each other. Reaper Of Reputation Aspect **Aspect's Agony** 1d6 persistent mental

The target must then attempt a DC 37 Will save.
**Critical Success** The target fails to hear the secret whispered and is unaffected.
**Success** The mask whispers a horrific secret to the target, and though their mind recoils and forgets, the target still takes 8d6 mental damage and is [frightened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76).
**Failure** As failure, but 17d6 mental damage and frightened 2; the target is [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=63) as long as they are frightened.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but 30d6 mental damage and the target is confused for 1 minute.
Masks and the Afterlife When a worshipper becomes a mask, they technically die and travel to the [Boneyard](/Planes.aspx?ID=39) to be judged by [Pharasma](/Deities.aspx?ID=290), but in this case, the process is almost instantaneous. When [Norgorber](/Deities.aspx?ID=289) chooses someone to become a mask, a swift and nearly instantaneous blurring of the creature is the only indication of their change. Like most fiends, masks are immortal unless slain through violence or misadventure. Once slain, a mask's body decays as normal, and after a variable amount of time has passed, their soul returns to the Great Beyond to accrete its quintessence into Norgorber's realm of Duskfathom.
Other Ancestries Most of the masks of Norgorber are [human](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=6), but not all. A mask's statistics don't change if it's a Small creature, and they gain [increased space and reach if they're Large or larger](/Rules.aspx?ID=2359). Change ancestry traits as needed, but Speed and languages are unchanged. All masks of Norgorber possess [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) granted them by their deity. Whether or not you grant a mask additional ancestry-based abilities is left to you to decide.

attacks.name: jaws
attacks.damage: 3d12+8 piercing plus 3d6 spirit and rabid rage

mid.name: Reaction Reversal
entries: Since an egarhowl appears to move backwards in time and the results of its actions manifest slightly out of sync, its manipulate or move actions and Strikes don't trigger reactions normally. Whenever a reaction would be triggered by an egarhowl in this way, the reacting creature must attempt a DC 11 flat check. On a failure, their reaction does not trigger.

mid.name: Predestined Defeat
entries: At the start of combat, an inverted, reversed explosion of spiritual and void energy implodes in a 30-foot emanation centered on the egarhowl—a reversal of the creature's spiritually explosive death. All creatures in the area take 6d8 spirit damage (DC 35 basic Fortitude save); creatures that fail this save are also slowed 1 for 1 round as time seems to distort around them.

mid.name: Rabid Rage
entries: An egarhowl's bite transmits its supernatural fury. A creature bitten by an egarhowl must attempt a DC 36 Will save. They then become temporarily immune to rabid rage for 24 hours.

mid.name: Critical Success
entries: The creature suffers no ill effects.

mid.name: Success
entries: The creature is filled with anger and becomes slowed 1 for 1 round as they waste some of their time shrieking and raving on their turn.

mid.name: Failure
entries: As success, but slowed 1 for 1 minute.

mid.name: Critical Failure
entries: As failure, but the creature is also confused for as long as it is slowed.

creature.name: Echosyvne

mid.name: Reaction Reversal
entries: Since an egarhowl appears to move backwards in time and the results of its actions manifest slightly out of sync, its manipulate or move actions and Strikes don't trigger reactions normally. Whenever a reaction would be triggered by an egarhowl in this way, the reacting creature must attempt a DC 11 flat check. On a failure, their reaction does not trigger.

mid.name: Predestined Defeat
entries: At the start of combat, an inverted, reversed explosion of spiritual and void energy implodes in a 30-foot emanation centered on the egarhowl—a reversal of the creature's spiritually explosive death. All creatures in the area take 15d8 spirit damage (DC 37 basic Fortitude save); creatures that fail this save are also slowed 1 for 1 round as time seems to distort around them.

mid.name: Distort Perception
entries: The echopsyvne targets a creature it can see within 30 feet and alters its perception of time. The target must attempt a DC 40 Will save. Regardless of success or failure, the creature then becomes temporarily immune to this ability for 24 hours.

mid.name: Critical Success
entries: The creature is unaffected.

mid.name: Success
entries: The creature perceives time to flow backward briefly and becomes slowed 1 for 1 round.

mid.name: Failure
entries: Time flows backward for the creature, leaving them unable to interact with the world around them. The creature is stunned 3, after which it is slowed 1 for 1 round.

mid.name: Critical Failure
entries: The creature's mind becomes stuck in a time loop, and it becomes paralyzed by the disorienting sight for 1 minute. At the end of each of its turns, it can attempt a new Will save to reduce the remaining duration by 1 round or end it entirely on a critical success.

mid.name: Temporal Possession
entries: When the echopsyvne casts possession on a creature, that creature experiences time backward. When the echopsyvne controls the target, they function normally, but when the target takes their own actions while the echopsyvne is in partial control or riding along in their body, they become clumsy 3 and take a –10-foot status penalty to all of their Speeds. When the echopsyvne stops possessing the target, willingly or otherwise, the target must succeed at a DC 37 Will save or be stunned 1 as they readjust to a more familiar flow of time.

creature.name: Venomfist

attacks.name: fist
attacks.damage: 4d6+21 bludgeoning plus 4d6 poison and Improved Grab

mid.name: Toxic Downpour
entries: Venomfist's presence alters the weather within 2 miles to heavy rainfall as long as they're located in a sizable body of water. When they become hostile, the rain in a 120-foot emanation from them becomes highly toxic and deals 8d8 poison damage (DC 42 basic Fortitude half) to all creatures in the area.

mid.name: Vortex
entries: 120 feet. Water in the area that is in the same body of water as Venomfist is difficult terrain for Swimming creatures that don't have the water trait.

mid.name: Create Poison
entries: Venomfist transforms a portion of their watery body into a single dose of any type of common poison of 20th level or lower—tears of death is their favorite. If they're holding a container, they can create the poison within that container, at which point the poison remains viable for 24 hours before it reverts to water. Alternatively, they can apply a contact or injury-created poison to their fist.

mid.name: Surge
entries: Venomfist expands their space to fill the area of their vortex. Creatures within the aura take 6d12+6 bludgeoning damage and 6d12+6 poison damage with a DC 45 basic Fortitude save. A creature that fails this save is pushed 40 feet. Venomfist then retracts to their former space and cannot use Surge again for 1d4 rounds.

_aon.markdown:
Before he became a deity, [Norgorber](/Deities.aspx?ID=289) gained Venomfist's eternal service by giving the disgraced [faydhaan shuyookh](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2662) poisons to exact revenge upon those who stripped the genie of their status. The vengeance transformed Venomfist into what they are now, an outcome Norgorber cautioned of, yet one Venomfist doesn't regret. Today in Duskfathom, Venomfist resides in the Sky Sea as the perfect defender of the unnamed islands. When summoned to other planes, only a part of them leaves while their main body remains behind. The zimiezeks, also known as those-that-weave-secrets, are one of many creatures native to Duskfathom. They resemble large spiders with humanoid hands instead of spidery feet and possess vaguely humanoid heads with multiple eyes and spider fangs for jaws. Their faces are often shrouded by a veil, mask, or webbing to both hide their identity and as a gesture of peace, for a zimiezek's bite can turn other humanoids into them. Unlike the [karumzeks](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=290), [Norgorber's](/Deities.aspx?ID=289) more common divine servitors, zimiezeks almost never leave Duskfathom. Most are average citizens who revere Norgorber as both deity and prince. Uncertain Origins The zimiezeks believe the first of them arose from souls who were once Norgorber's allies in life who stumbled upon the god's greatest secret and were slain to conceal his identity. Some doubt this claim, given Norgorber's anathema on showing mercy. Nevertheless, a connection exists between Norgorber and both zimiezeks and karumzeks that lets the god automatically know the creatures' names and identities.
